title: New wrap-bound rejection row can never fail — vacuous harness, and the value/rule pair is wrong even under a repaired harness
evidence: core/catalog_test.odin:887: {"box interval over the wrap bound", replace1(BAL_VALID, `"dot_interval_ticks": 2400`, `"dot_interval_ticks": 1099511627776`, 1), "must be <= 2^40 (the HUD permille math's wrap bound)"} | core/catalog_test.odin:1000-1008 (check_reject_balance's Catalog_Sources has NO crises field): node_types   = transmute([]u8)string(NT_VALID), ... eras       = transmute([]u8)string(ERAS_VALID), } / cerr := catalogs_load(cat, &src) / if cerr.file != "balance.json" { testing.expectf(t, cerr.file != "", ...) return } | core/catalog.odin:736+746 (crises block parses BEFORE balance; 'crises.json', '$', 'invalid JSON') vs core/catalog.odin:907+910 (balance block) | core/catalog.odin:1813: jint_strict :: proc(o: json.Object, key: string, def: i32) -> (i32, bool) | core/catalog.odin:1157: return {"balance.json", "box", "clock keys must be integers (no decimals)"} | core/catalog.odin:1168-1169: if u64(di) > u64(1) << 40 { return {"balance.json", "box", "dot_interval_ticks must be <= 2^40 (the HUD permille math's wrap bound)"}
detail: check_reject_balance omits crises, so catalogs_load aborts at crises.json (parsed before balance.json) and the harness passes trivially on the non-empty file name. Even repaired, 1099511627776 == 2^40 fails the strict '>' guard, and jint_strict's i32 rejects it earlier as 'clock keys must be integers' — never the expected substring. The row (claimed as N12 coverage in commit 7208ec5) and the whole bal_rows table are vacuous; the 2^40 guard itself is unreachable dead code via i32.
recommended_fix: Pass a valid crises doc (CRISES_VALID) in check_reject_balance's Catalog_Sources; use an out-of-i32 value and assert the 'clock keys must be integers' rule, or widen jint_strict/the interval read to i64 so the 2^40 guard is reachable, then verify RED-then-GREEN.

title: dots_post_crisis counts from first crisis ACTIVATION, not 'after the last crisis resolved'
evidence: harness/econ.odin:43: dots_post_crisis: i32, // dots AFTER the last crisis resolved (the no-death-spiral recovery) | harness/econ.odin:90: if stats.saw_crisis_active do stats.dots_post_crisis += 1 | harness/econ.odin:94: if len(s.crisis.active) > 0 do stats.saw_crisis_active = true
detail: saw_crisis_active latches at first activation and is never cleared, so dots landing MID-crisis also count toward the no-death-spiral check; the comment claims post-resolution only. The [floor, base] interval pins still hold the guarantee, so this weakens the diagnostic's description, not the gate.
recommended_fix: Recomment as 'dots after the first crisis became active' or reset saw_crisis_active when crisis.active empties to measure true post-resolution recovery.
